RNClientIoShutdown is an additive bounded ownership abstraction for sdk/rocketnet_client_transport.cpp (rocketnet_client_transport_stop, rocketnet_client_transport_stopped and rocketnet_client_transport_destroy): RequestStop publishes the final filling ring while another is sending; RequestReturn and PollReturn do not depend on worker progress; WorkerQuiesce follows ring drain and key wipe; WorkerExit, Join and Free separate completion from final thread ownership. CompletionMeansQuiescent, FreedOnlyAfterJoin, NoReuseBeforeComplete, RequestNeverWaits and PollNeverWaits cover the intended sequence, with stuck-worker and six reversed witnesses. The same request/completion contract applies to the public client/server and both transports, but this model is not a refinement or composition of their data-path models and does not prove native cancellation, C++ atomic ordering, callback termination, platform cleanup or latency; exact implementation and platform qualification remain separate. Environment actions Done. Done is a terminal stutter.

RNUringDriver models the io_uring server driver in sdk/rocketnet_server_uring_linux.cpp (one ring on the main thread, no worker thread): Reserve is rocketnet_server_uring_start_packet (one fetch_add, NULL when full); Finish(s) is rocketnet_server_uring_finish_packet and Abort(s) is rocketnet_server_uring_abort_packet (the slot from rocketnet_server_uring_slot); Submit, Reap and ResetIndex are rocketnet_server_uring_send_packets (one SENDMSG per send run of slots with bytes: with UDP_SEGMENT a run of consecutive equal-size slots to one destination, the last allowed shorter, built by rocketnet_uring_gso_message in sdk/rocketnet_uring_codec.h with a UDP_SEGMENT cmsg, one slot otherwise; submitted in chunks no larger than the free SQ space, reaped until every send of the call has its CQE, then the index reset to 0); KernelComplete(s), KernelFill(b) and KernelStop are the kernel posting send, receive and final (no F_MORE) CQEs, a receive buffer holding one to Segments datagrams (with UDP_GRO, probed all or nothing at create, one coalesced receive), a send CQE named by its run's head slot and freeing every slot of the run; Reap(c) is rocketnet_server_uring_reap_cqe by tag kind (send, recv, cancel), the recv case rocketnet_server_uring_receive_cqe splitting the buffer at its UDP_GRO stride (rocketnet_uring_recvmsg_parse, rocketnet_coalesce_split) and copying every segment into the fill bank whether reaped from receive_packets or inside send_packets, and the term case re-arming through rocketnet_server_uring_arm unless destroying; ReturnBuffer(b) is the io_uring_buf_ring_add at the end of rocketnet_server_uring_receive_cqe, after the last segment is copied (ReturnAfterLastCopy); Swap is rocketnet_server_uring_receive_packets and TransportReads is rocketnet_server_uring_process_packets; Destroy and Free are rocketnet_server_uring_destroy (cancel every multishot, wait for each cancel CQE and each multishot's last CQE, then free the buffer rings, the ring, the sockets and the memory); invariants TypeOK, NoReuseWhileKernelOwned, ExposedStable, BufferReturnedAfterCopy and FreedOnlyWhenDrained, liveness SubmittedEventuallyFree and DestroyEventuallyFrees under SpecFair; passing control MCRNUringDriver.cfg and reversed witnesses MCRNUringDriverBrokenResetBeforeReap.cfg (NoReuseWhileKernelOwned), MCRNUringDriverBrokenOneBank.cfg (ExposedStable), MCRNUringDriverBrokenFreeRunAtSubmit.cfg (NoReuseWhileKernelOwned: a run's slots after its head handed back at Submit) and MCRNUringDriverBrokenReturnBeforeSplit.cfg (BufferReturnedAfterCopy: a coalesced buffer returned once its first segment is copied). Where the code refines the model: one multishot per queue rather than one; Submit runs in chunks interleaved with Reap, with sends in flight capped at ROCKETNET_URING_ENTRIES; a cancel that finds no request is sent again; Destroy requires stopped: rocketnet_server_uring_stop marks destroying, rocketnet_server_uring_stopped cancels every multishot and reaps until no send, cancel or multishot remains, and only then rocketnet_server_uring_destroy frees the buffer rings, the ring, the sockets and the memory, so FreedOnlyWhenDrained holds because Free never runs while the kernel owns a buffer. Exercised by test_server_uring_probe (including the stalled-completion branch through rocketnet_server_uring_test_stall_destroy), test_server_uring_wire_ipv4, test_io_uring_transport_server_wire_gso_ipv4, _wire_gso_ipv6, _wire_plain, _wire_gro_ipv4 and _wire_gro_ipv6 (tests/functional/rocketnet_functional_tests.cpp), test_uring_gso_message_stride_and_tail and test_uring_recvmsg_gro_stride (tests/test_unit_uring_codec.cpp). ServerConnection models the encryption map keyed by source address that this hashed table holds: capacity-sized slots with a per-bucket chain and a free list, add assigning the free head, remove unlinking and zeroing the mapping, find walking the bucket and next returning live slots in index order. The DST checks acked_means_opened (the server's rocketnet_encryption_map_find and rocketnet_encryption_map_entry join key) and stale_session_payload (rocketnet_encryption_map_address of a connected slot's mapping) read the map through the real server protocol in every seed.

ServerSession (ResetIsInit, SlotReuseObservesNothing) and ClientSession (ResetIsInit, ReconnectObservesNothing) model the per-connection reset this file performs: the client reset retiring keys and wiping the connection before restoring counters, rate, filter and callbacks, the server reset removing the mapping before releasing the slot so the mapping is wiped while the slot still identifies it, and the message-layer reset keeping the disconnect reason across a fresh endpoint region. The DST checks stale_session_payload and one_session_per_slot observe a reused slot and a reconnected client delivering nothing of the old session.

ServerSession (SlotOwnsItsSession, TokenAdmitsOnce) models the server slot table this file holds: client ids hashed into per-bucket chains with the next links, the free stack filled highest-first so the first assigns pop 0, 1, 2 in order, connect binding a client id and disconnect pushing the index back. The DST checks one_session_per_slot and token_admits_once read rocketnet_client_slots_client_id and rocketnet_client_slots_connected through the real server protocol in every seed.

No model: no state. The file is two pure key derivations over fixed 8-byte KDF contexts, crypto_generichash with a 32-byte token key over at most 112 input bytes, with the shared secret and the input wiped after use; a model adds nothing to a function of its arguments, and the outputs are pinned by the standard key schedule and handshake vectors in test_unit_standard_key_schedule.cpp, test_unit_standard_handshake_client.cpp and test_unit_standard_handshake_server.cpp.

No model: the counter law is an arithmetic identity, not a state machine. The tables are generated from the row list so an index, name, class and family cannot drift, and rocketnet_counters_conserved holds when every RECEIVED counter equals the sum of its family. The DST checks conservation (called for the server and the clients at the last step of every seed) and unexplained_refusal (every nonzero refusal counter is in the explained table) cover it.

No model: platform frame pacing, not protocol state. The pure parts are unit-tested directly (sdk/rocketnet_tests.cpp: rocketnet_frame_sync_guard_ns, rocketnet_frame_sync_adapt_guard and rocketnet_frame_sync_advance, no wall clock), and the remaining code is the platform clock and absolute sleep plus the waiting thread's priority, a functional concern of the platform tier with no protocol invariant a TLA+ model could refine.

RNBufferHandoff models the N-buffer handoff of sdk/rocketnet_buffer_handoff.h as the client transport uses it in both directions (docs/decisions/BUFFER-HANDOFF-DECISION-20261021.md): N preallocated buffers, each owned by exactly one of the producer, the ready queue, the consumer and the free queue; only indices move, inside a mutex held for the exchange alone; the game thread only try-acquires it and never waits; the I/O thread acquires it and waits on a level-triggered wake. It supersedes the two-ring send state machine and the two-buffer receive handshake of RNClientIo, whose remaining actions (destinations, wait and wake, stop and join) still describe the design. The I/O core sends committed slots, finishes a sent ring, receives, publishes or owes, waits, wakes, clears a wake and exits. Steps IoSend, IoFinishRing, IoReceive, IoPublish, IoOwe, IoWait, IoWake, IoClearWake and IoExit.
The I/O core receives, publishes or owes, waits, wakes and clears a wake, and exposes and returns the held buffer. Steps IoReceive, IoPublish, IoOwe, IoWait, IoWake, IoClearWake, Expose and Return.
The I/O worker waits and wakes, exchanges a buffer, stops and exits. Steps WorkerWait, WorkerWakes, ConsumerExchange, ProducerExchange, MainStop and WorkerExit.
The I/O send loop finishes a sent ring, takes the next ring, and the quit path exits the worker. Steps FinishRing, TakeRing and WorkerExit.

Commit writes every forget and then every mark into the kernel map in one commit. A forget the kernel refuses (anything but a missing key; a refused batch delete is walked one element at a time) stays pending at the front of the buffer and is applied first in the next commit (rocketnet_xdp_replay_marks_reset_keeping), invariant ForgetOwedUntilApplied, reversed witness MCRNXdpReplayBrokenFailedForgetDropped.cfg (ForgetOwedUntilApplied); a kept forget whose key a mark applied in the same commit is superseded and dropped (mark_applied; a refused batch update is walked one element at a time), so a retry never deletes a newer session's mark, invariant RetryNeverDeletesNewerMark, reversed witness MCRNXdpReplayBrokenSupersededForget.cfg (RetryNeverDeletesNewerMark); a mark the kernel refuses (a refused batch update is walked one element at a time) stays pending at the front of the mark list and is applied again in the next commit, a newer mark of its key replacing it in place and a queued forget of its key dropping it, invariant MarkOwedUntilApplied, reversed witnesses MCRNXdpReplayBrokenRefusedMarkDropped.cfg (MarkOwedUntilApplied) and MCRNXdpReplayBrokenKeptMarkAfterForget.cfg (ForgetOwedUntilApplied); until a new session's kept or unqueued zero mark lands, rocketnet_server_socket_hold_greetings drops its keep-alives at publish (HoldGreetingUntilMarked, NewSessionNeverDroppedByOldMark, reversed witness MCRNXdpReplayBrokenGreetBeforeMark.cfg); the buffer's refusals are added to the commit failure count. Queue acceptance also drops the learned reply MAC; queue refusal leaves the server slot responsible, while a later kernel delete refusal remains owned by the pending buffer.
Connect starts a session with the opened high water at zero. UserOpen raises that high water on a genuine session packet.
Release ends the session for the slot being cleared.
The maintenance pass walks marks and then commits them. Steps Walk and Commit.

The walk is rocketnet_server_replay_marks_walk: the forget pass forgets the address of every slot that was seen connected and is no longer connected or whose mapping address changed, whether or not it held a mark, and the mark pass marks every connected slot whose highest_opened changed (none counting as zero) and every slot it first sees, zero included, so a reconnect between two walks or into another slot replaces the old session's entry (NewSessionNeverDroppedByOldMark, reversed witness MCRNXdpReplayBrokenReconnectFreshness.cfg), and records every connected slot with a mapping as seen at its address. and a mark the sink cannot queue leaves the cache and sets the slot's mark_owed, so the next walk takes it again (AdvanceOnQueueRefusal, MarkOwedUntilApplied, reversed witness MCRNXdpReplayBrokenQueueRefusedAdvances.cfg). Steps Walk and Commit.

The reply MAC table with no gateway: rocketnet_xdp_reply_mac, called by the xdp start with the source MAC of the frame a direct response answers, addresses the reply by it and keeps it as the address's answered entry (rocketnet_xdp_reply_macs_answer), step Answer; a reply with no frame in hand, among them one the development link simulator held and its duplicate (rocketnet_server_link_drain in sdk/rocketnet_server_transport.cpp), takes the learned MAC, else its own address's answered entry, else it is refused and counted as SEND_NO_LINK_ADDRESS, step Drain; a learn takes the answered entry's slot (rocketnet_xdp_reply_macs_learn), step Connect, and a forget leaves the learned MAC as the answered entry (rocketnet_xdp_reply_macs_forget), step Commit. The link holding a reply is outside the code: environment actions HoldSessionReply and HoldStray.
Connect leaves the replay window unchanged when a session takes a slot.

A taken sequence is spent unsent when the frame is refused, a seal refusal after the fragment reservation spends the fragmented start, and the outbox goes on the wire in fill order. Steps BurnOne, BurnFragmented and Flush.

A taken sequence is spent unsent when the seal fails, a seal refusal after the fragment reservation spends the fragmented start, and the staged packets go on the wire in fill order. Steps BurnOne, BurnFragmented and Flush.

The message object begins and ends an update, rejects an update while a view is held, kicks, resets a freed slot, observes bindings, feeds acks and opens, requests and starts, finishes, sends and releases. Steps BeginUpdate, EndUpdate, RejectUnreleasedUpdate, Kick, ResetFree, Observe, TransportAck, TransportOpen, Request, StartPending, FinishPending, Send and Release.
PublicDisconnect ends one slot or every slot from the public entry.
Connect gives the slot its connection id when the session is accepted.
Disconnect returns the slot connection id to none.
Add inserts a live mapping. Remove drops that mapping and wipes its secrets.
Add copies user data into a slot as it becomes live. Remove clears that user data and returns the slot to the free list.
Remove wipes the mapping secrets and then clears the slot user data.
WriteAck sends a packet that carries only the owed acks when that debt is nonzero.
WriteAck sends a packet that carries only the owed acks.
DropUnreliableForBudget drops an unreliable packet that does not fit the budget and counts it.
DropUnreliableForBudget drops unreliable sends past the budget and counts them, and that pass writes nothing further.
Take hands the application the next delivery and advances the queue.

Enqueue assigns ordering and sequencing counters as a message joins the queue. WriteAny is the packet write of any message on either attempt. ArriveFragment collects a block's fragments by index as they arrive.
MemoryExhausted ends the connection when the send region has no room left.
AckAny retires the reliable send of one acked packet id.
Send issues the next receipt serial before any packet write. SweepLoss is the receipt deadline on the same file.
OpenPacket is the far-end dispatch of a packet, marking it opened.
NumberRecord numbers a reliable record into the send window. ReceiveAck advances the oldest unacked number.
OpenPacket accepts one record into the receive window. EndUpdate releases a live number.
The server transport update fixes the received batch before this update sends any reply. Step FixBatch.
SendAck builds the ack block of every session packet from the opened packet ids and clears the ack debt. Step SendAck.
The server transport update fixes the received batch before this update sends any reply. Step FixBatch.
SendAck builds the ack block of every session packet and clears the ack debt after the batch is fixed. Step SendAck.

rocketnet_server_socket_finish_packet completes the packet slot that XdpStart staged in the producer buffer: it writes the byte count of that slot, and it refuses a packet pointer outside the current producer buffer, through rocketnet_server_socket_send_slot, so a pointer from before the last Publish flip is a lost packet and never rewrites a published one. Actions XdpStart and Publish.

MainStop hands the final producer to TX; Consume and WorkerExit send every published bank and the final producer before exit.
